answer: Each identity lives in a ferrous vault, a TPM chip whose key never leaves it. Joining needs a signed pearl proving the vault is real, and one chip makes one identity. Seven auditors spot-check quotes weekly and re-check flagged ones. A fake quote triggers a ripple audit of its batch, burning every bond in it. One honest agent pays $25 for the chip and a $50 bond, refunded later. A hundred clones need a hundred chips and $5,000 in bonds, and one caught fake torches the whole batch, so a hundred clones cost $12,500 against $2,500 honest. A fingerprint pressed into iron fits only one hand.
